20 REMARK OF ASSESSMENT (INCLUDING FINAL EXAMINATION)
20.1 A student may appeal the decision to disallow the re-mark of an assessment to the Deputy Vice
Chancellor, Academic.
20.2 Grounds for appeal: The Student may appeal on any grounds that show that the Course
Coordinator failed to follow due process in accordance with the Procedure: Assessment and
Examinations s and / or a Course Outline.
20.3 Timing for lodging appeal: The Student must lodge the appeal within 10 Working Days of the
date the Student received notice of the decision. The Deputy Vice Chancellor, Academic may
extend the time for lodging the appeal in exceptional circumstances.
20.4 Timing for University review of appeal: The Deputy Vice Chancellor, Academic will review and
determine the appeal within 20 Working Days of receiving the appeal.
20.5 Notification: The Deputy Vice Chancellor, Academic will advise the Student and the decision-
maker in writing of the determination, in accordance with the requirements for notification set
out in section 6.5 of this policy.
20.6 Further appeal: The decision of the Deputy Vice Chancellor, Academic is final and not open to
further internal appeal.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Attributable human/group responsibility and traceable disclosure of relevant AI assistance. Access differences become critical where a required tool blocks participation without a workable alternative.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N026 (6.2.1) requires identifiable individual contributions and fair workload in group work, N028 (4.5.2.3) prohibits unauthorised Gen-AI, and the scenario does not involve a required paid tool blocking participation without a workable alternative.
case_summary.case_note: Procedure: Assessment and Examinations (N026, 6.2.1) requires group assessments to identify individual contributions and resolve group issues, while N028 (4.5.2.3) conditions generative AI use on express authorisation. Although paid AI access disparities within groups are not explicitly regulated, the existing rules establish structured discretion without a critical gap; Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
